subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Dribbling, Passing, and Foot Skills in Small-Sided Play
title: Guided practice B: small-sided cooperative play
essentialQuestion: How do I keep and move an object as a team?
materials: unit equipment listed in the guardian safety review
movementCues: Fewer players means more touches for everyone.
Agree rules and boundaries before starting.
Cooperate towards a shared target rather than a winner.
commonErrorToWatchFor: One player dominating possession. Fix: require every player to touch the ball before the team target counts.
keyPoints: Fewer players means more touches for everyone.
Agree rules and boundaries before starting.
Cooperate towards a shared target rather than a winner.
privacySafeScenario: Play a small-sided cooperative game and explain two decisions you made about space and support.
studentTask: The learner practises small-sided cooperative play at a self-selected challenge level, using the adapted alternative whenever it fits better, and names the cue that helped.
knowledgeCheck: The learner names one cue that helped with small-sided cooperative play and one adjustment for next time, by demonstrating, describing, drawing, or writing.
completionCriteria: The learner takes part in the task about small-sided cooperative play at a self-selected challenge level.
The learner uses or names the movement cues for small-sided cooperative play.
The learner identifies one adjustment or next step. No score, time, count, or measurement is required.
adaptationChoices: Foot-skill tasks may be done with a stationary ball, a slower rolled ball, a larger ball, a hand or assistive device in place of the foot, or from a seated position. Travel distance is always adjustable.
extensionChallenge: Apply small-sided cooperative play under one new condition of the learner choosing — different equipment, space, speed, or partner — and describe what changed.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show or describe a model before practice.
Allow demonstrated, described, drawn, spoken, signed, or written evidence; the response mode is never the standard being assessed.
Offer reduced-repetition, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-stimulation options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Preserve the movement target while adjusting equipment, distance, speed, force, duration, or support.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to enjoy one safe, optional activity that practises small-sided cooperative play. No purchase, account creation, recording, measurement, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
